minutes.headline: Committee voted to advertise the town manager job on MMA, GovHR and ICMA; the final ad wording waits a week.
minutes.summary: The Town Manager Screening Committee approved prior minutes, heard reports on where to advertise, and debated hiring a retained recruiter. It voted to post on GovHR and ICMA in addition to MMA, and one member will interview recruiters. After long debate on the job ad and a member's alternative job description, it chose to wait a week to finalize both the ad and a website posting.

what_happened.line: The Town Manager Screening Committee voted 4-0 by roll call to advertise the town manager job on GovHR and ICMA as well as MMA.
Members chose to try the three advertising venues first and revisit a retained recruiter in a few weeks if results are poor; one member will interview recruiters.
After long debate on the ad wording, salary range and a member's alternative job description, the committee decided to wait a week to finalize both.
The Beacon ad slips to September, and the chair will ask the select board chair to add a salary range discussion to a special meeting agenda.

why_it_matters: The ad, and whether a search firm is hired, shape who applies to run the town's day-to-day operations, so the delay in wording and timing pushes back when candidates can start applying.
No approved salary range exists yet, and the pay offered will be set through the select board, which affects the cost of the position that goes into a future town budget.
watch_next: The committee's next meeting in a week, where the ad and the alternative job description are due to be finalized.
The select board's special meeting agenda, to see whether a salary range discussion is added.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree that the committee settled on advertising with MMA, ICMA and GovHR, and that the ad was not ready to place. They differ on whether that vote passed, on who was to look into recruiters, and on a long list of figures and decisions that only our recording-based minutes carry.
